questions.text: Which of the following is not the criterion for similarity of triangles?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not the criterion for similarity of triangles?
questions.solution: RHS (Right Angle-Hypotenuse-Side) is a criterion for congruence of triangles, not similarity. The criteria for similarity of triangles are AAA, SSS, and SAS.

questions.text: From the figures given below, which of the following is true about the measure of ∠P?
questions.text_english: From the figures given below, which of the following is true about the measure of ∠P?
questions.image_description: Two triangles are shown. Triangle ABC has angle A = 80°, angle B = 60°, AB = 3.8 cm, BC = 6 cm, AC = 3√3 cm. Triangle RPQ has RP = 6√3 cm, RQ = 7.6 cm, PQ = 12 cm. The triangles appear to be similar.

options.D: The measure of ∠P cannot be determined

options_english.D: The measure of ∠P cannot be determined

questions.solution: In triangle ABC: angle A = 80°, angle B = 60°, so angle C = 40°. Checking the sides: AB/PQ = 3.8/12, BC/QR is not simply proportional, but AC/PR = 3√3 / 6√3 = 1/2 and BC/PQ = 6/12 = 1/2. Since the ratio of corresponding sides are equal and the included angles match (SAS similarity or SSS), triangle ABC ~ triangle CPQ (or appropriate correspondence). By the correspondence, ∠P corresponds to ∠C = 40°. Hence ∠P = 40°.

questions.text: If the distance of a tangent to a circle from its centre is 4 cm, then the length of diameter of the circle is:
questions.text_english: If the distance of a tangent to a circle from its centre is 4 cm, then the length of diameter of the circle is:
questions.solution: The distance from the centre to a tangent is equal to the radius of the circle. So radius = 4 cm. Diameter = 2 × radius = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements is false?
questions.solution: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2. Since 1/2 ≠ √3/2, the statement sin 30° = cos 30° is false. The other options: tan 45° = cot 45° = 1 (true); sin 90° = 1 = tan 45° (true); sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2 (true).

questions.text: The value of (cot² A − 1/sin² A) is:
questions.text_english: The value of (cot² A − 1/sin² A) is:
questions.solution: cot² A − 1/sin² A = cos²A/sin²A − 1/sin²A = (cos²A − 1)/sin²A = −sin²A/sin²A = −1.

questions.text: In the given figure, which of the following angles represents the angle of depression?
questions.text_english: In the given figure, which of the following angles represents the angle of depression?
questions.image_description: A figure showing an observer at the top left, a horizontal dashed line extending to the right, with angles z (between the horizontal and the line of sight going down-right) and y below z, and at the base a vertical line with angle a and at the object position angle x. The line of sight goes from observer diagonally down to an object.
questions.solution: The angle of depression is the angle between the horizontal line (from the observer's eye) and the line of sight going downward to the object. In the figure, this is angle z.

questions.text: The perimeter of the shaded region in the given figure is:
questions.text_english: The perimeter of the shaded region in the given figure is:
questions.image_description: A circle with centre O. Inside the circle, an isosceles triangle is formed with two equal sides of length r (radii), and base a. The shaded region is the triangle. The arc length corresponding to the triangle is l. The shaded region appears to be the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord a.
questions.solution: The shaded region is bounded by the arc (length l), two radii (each of length r), and the chord/base (length a). Therefore, perimeter = l + r + r + a = l + 2r + a.

questions.text: The ratio of the area of a quadrant of a circle to the area of the same circle is:
questions.text_english: The ratio of the area of a quadrant of a circle to the area of the same circle is:
questions.solution: Area of quadrant = (1/4)πr². Area of full circle = πr². Ratio = (1/4)πr² : πr² = 1 : 4.

questions.text: For which of the following solids is the lateral/curved surface area and total surface area the same?
questions.text_english: For which of the following solids is the lateral/curved surface area and total surface area the same?
questions.solution: For a sphere: Curved surface area = 4πr² and Total surface area = 4πr². They are the same because a sphere has no flat faces. For a cube, cuboid, and hemisphere, the lateral/curved surface area is different from the total surface area (which includes the flat base/faces).

questions.text:
The class mark of the median class of the following data is:

| Class Interval | 10–25 | 25–40 | 40–55 | 55–70 | 70–85 | 85–100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 3 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
questions.text_english:
The class mark of the median class of the following data is:

| Class Interval | 10–25 | 25–40 | 40–55 | 55–70 | 70–85 | 85–100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 3 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
questions.solution: Total frequency = 2+3+7+6+6+6 = 30. N/2 = 15. Cumulative frequencies: up to 25 = 2, up to 40 = 5, up to 55 = 12, up to 70 = 18. Since cumulative frequency first exceeds 15 in the class 55–70... wait: up to 55 = 12 < 15 and up to 70 = 18 ≥ 15. So the median class is 40–55. Class mark = (40+55)/2 = 47.5.

questions.text:
The following distribution shows the number of runs scored by some batsmen in test matches:

| Runs Scored | 3000–4000 | 4000–5000 | 5000–6000 | 6000–7000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of Batsmen | 5 | 10 | 9 | 8 |

The lower limit of the modal class is:
questions.text_english:
The following distribution shows the number of runs scored by some batsmen in test matches:

| Runs Scored | 3000–4000 | 4000–5000 | 5000–6000 | 6000–7000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of Batsmen | 5 | 10 | 9 | 8 |

The lower limit of the modal class is:
questions.solution: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. Frequencies: 5, 10, 9, 8. The highest frequency is 10, which belongs to the class 4000–5000. Therefore the lower limit of the modal class is 4000.

questions.text: A bag contains 3 red, 4 white and 7 green balls. A ball is drawn at random. The probability that the ball drawn is not of red colour is:
questions.text_english: A bag contains 3 red, 4 white and 7 green balls. A ball is drawn at random. The probability that the ball drawn is not of red colour is:
questions.solution: Total balls = 3 + 4 + 7 = 14. Balls not red = 4 + 7 = 11. P(not red) = 11/14.

questions.text: If the HCF of two positive integers a and b is 1, then their LCM is:
questions.text_english: If the HCF of two positive integers a and b is 1, then their LCM is:
questions.solution: We know that HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. If HCF = 1, then LCM = a × b = ab.

(√3 − 3)/√3 = √3/√3 − 3/√3 = 1 − 3/√3 = 1 − √3. Since √3 is irrational, 1 − √3 is irrational. Wait: let's recalculate. (√3 − 3)/√3 = 1 − 3/√3 = 1 − 3·(1/√3) = 1 − 3·(√3/3) = 1 − √3. This is irrational. Hence the answer is (B) an irrational number.

questions.text: The discriminant of the quadratic equation −x² − 5x + 6 = 0 is:
questions.text_english: The discriminant of the quadratic equation −x² − 5x + 6 = 0 is:
questions.solution: For the equation −x² − 5x + 6 = 0, a = −1, b = −5, c = 6. Discriminant = b² − 4ac = (−5)² − 4(−1)(6) = 25 + 24 = 49.

questions.text: The equation x + 1/x = 3 (x ≠ 0) is expressed as a quadratic equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. The value of a − b + c is:
questions.text_english: The equation x + 1/x = 3 (x ≠ 0) is expressed as a quadratic equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. The value of a − b + c is:
questions.solution: x + 1/x = 3 → multiply both sides by x: x² + 1 = 3x → x² − 3x + 1 = 0. So a = 1, b = −3, c = 1. a − b + c = 1 − (−3) + 1 = 1 + 3 + 1 = 5.

questions.text: The distance of a point P(3, −7) from y-axis is:
questions.text_english: The distance of a point P(3, −7) from y-axis is:
questions.solution: The distance of a point (x, y) from the y-axis is |x|. For P(3, −7), the distance = |3| = 3.

questions.text: The mid-point of a line segment divides the line segment in the ratio:
questions.text_english: The mid-point of a line segment divides the line segment in the ratio:
questions.solution: By definition, the mid-point divides the line segment into two equal parts. Therefore, the ratio is 1 : 1.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The value of p for which the system of equations 4x + py + 8 = 0 and 2x + 2y + 2 = 0 is consistent is 4.

Reason (R): The system of equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ is consistent with infinitely many solutions, if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The value of p for which the system of equations 4x + py + 8 = 0 and 2x + 2y + 2 = 0 is consistent is 4.

Reason (R): The system of equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ is consistent with infinitely many solutions, if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: For the system 4x + py + 8 = 0 and 2x + 2y + 2 = 0: a₁/a₂ = 4/2 = 2, b₁/b₂ = p/2, c₁/c₂ = 8/2 = 4. For consistency with infinitely many solutions: 2 = p/2 = 4 → p/2 = 2 → p = 4, but c₁/c₂ = 4 ≠ 2. So the system with p = 4 gives 4/2 = 4/2 ≠ 8/2, meaning it is actually inconsistent (parallel lines). The system is consistent (unique solution) when a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, i.e., p ≠ 4. So Assertion A is false (p = 4 does NOT make it consistent). Reason R is true (correct condition for infinitely many solutions). Hence answer is D.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): For any two natural numbers a and b, the HCF of a and b is a factor of the LCM of a and b.

Reason (R): HCF of any two natural numbers divides both the numbers.
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): For any two natural numbers a and b, the HCF of a and b is a factor of the LCM of a and b.

Reason (R): HCF of any two natural numbers divides both the numbers.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b, so HCF divides LCM. Reason R is also true: HCF divides both a and b by definition. However, R does not directly explain A (A follows from the relation HCF × LCM = a × b, not just from the fact that HCF divides both numbers). Hence both are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.text: Two concentric circles are of radii 6 cm and 10 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.
questions.text_english: Two concentric circles are of radii 6 cm and 10 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.

key_points: Let the chord AB of the larger circle (radius 10 cm) be tangent to the smaller circle (radius 6 cm).
The perpendicular from the centre O to the chord bisects it. Let the foot of perpendicular be M.
OM = 6 cm (radius of smaller circle, since chord is tangent to it).
By Pythagoras theorem: AM² = OA² − OM² = 100 − 36 = 64, so AM = 8 cm.
Length of chord AB = 2 × AM = 16 cm.

questions.solution: Let the chord AB of the larger circle be tangent to the smaller circle. The perpendicular from centre O to AB bisects it at M, and OM = 6 cm (radius of smaller circle). OA = 10 cm. By Pythagoras: AM = √(10² − 6²) = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm. So AB = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

अथवा

sub_questions.text: Find the values of A and B (0 ≤ A < 90°, 0 ≤ B < 90°), if tan (A + B) = 1 and tan (A − B) = 1/√3.
sub_questions.text_english: Find the values of A and B (0 ≤ A < 90°, 0 ≤ B < 90°), if tan (A + B) = 1 and tan (A − B) = 1/√3.
sub_questions.solution: tan(A+B) = 1 = tan 45°, so A+B = 45°. tan(A−B) = 1/√3 = tan 30°, so A−B = 30°. Adding: 2A = 75°, A = 37.5°. Subtracting: 2B = 15°, B = 7.5°.

sub_questions.text_english: Prove that tan 45° = 1 geometrically.

key_points: Consider a right-angled triangle ABC with angle B = 90° and angle A = 45°.
Since angle A = angle C = 45°, the sides opposite to them are equal: BC = AB.

sub_questions.solution: Consider right triangle ABC with angle B = 90°, angle A = 45°. Then angle C = 45° as well. Since angles A and C are equal, the opposite sides are equal: BC = AB. tan 45° = BC/AB = 1.

questions.text: दी गई आकृति में, दो संकेंद्रीय वृत्त जिनके केन्द्र O तथा त्रिज्याएँ 2 cm और 3 cm हैं, दिखाए गए हैं। छायांकित भाग का परिमाप ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In the given figure, two concentric circles with centre O and radii 2 cm and 3 cm are shown. Find the perimeter of the shaded region.
questions.image_description: Two concentric circles with centre O. The inner circle has radius 2 cm and outer circle has radius 3 cm. A sector of 60° is shown. The shaded region is the area between the two circles within the 60° sector (an arc-shaped region).

key_points: The shaded region is bounded by two arcs (one from each circle) and two radial line segments.
Arc length of outer circle (r=3, θ=60°) = (60/360) × 2π × 3 = π cm
Arc length of inner circle (r=2, θ=60°) = (60/360) × 2π × 2 = 2π/3 cm
Two straight line segments each of length = 3 − 2 = 1 cm

questions.solution: The shaded region (sector annulus) is bounded by: arc of outer circle = (60°/360°) × 2π(3) = π cm; arc of inner circle = (60°/360°) × 2π(2) = 2π/3 cm; two straight segments of length (3−2) = 1 cm each. Perimeter = π + 2π/3 + 2 = 3π/3 + 2π/3 + 2 = 5π/3 + 2 cm.

questions.text_english:
Solve for x and y:
0.1x + 0.3y = 1
0.2x − 0.1y = −0.1

key_points: Multiply both equations by 10: x + 3y = 10 and 2x − y = −1.
From equation 2: y = 2x + 1. Substitute into equation 1: x + 3(2x+1) = 10 → x + 6x + 3 = 10 → 7x = 7 → x = 1.

questions.solution: Multiplying both equations by 10: x + 3y = 10 ...(1) and 2x − y = −1 ...(2). From (2): y = 2x + 1. Substituting in (1): x + 3(2x+1) = 10 → 7x = 7 → x = 1. y = 3. So x = 1, y = 3.

questions.text: सिद्ध कीजिए कि वृत्त के परिगत बना आयत एक वर्ग होता है।
questions.text_english: Prove that a rectangle circumscribing a circle is a square.

key_points: Let ABCD be a rectangle circumscribing a circle. Let the circle touch the sides AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R, S respectively.
Tangents from an external point to a circle are equal. From A: AP = AS. From B: BP = BQ. From C: CQ = CR. From D: DR = DS.
AB = AP + PB, BC = BQ + QC, CD = CR + RD, DA = DS + SA.
AB = AP + BP = AS + BQ. CD = CR + RD = CQ + DS.
AB + CD = AS + BQ + CQ + DS = AD + BC.
For a rectangle, AB = CD and BC = DA, so 2AB = 2BC → AB = BC.
Since all sides are equal and all angles are 90°, ABCD is a square.

questions.solution: Let ABCD be a rectangle circumscribing a circle touching sides at P, Q, R, S. By equal tangents: AP=AS, BP=BQ, CQ=CR, DR=DS. Thus AB+CD = (AP+BP)+(CR+DR) = (AS+BQ)+(CQ+DS) = (AS+DS)+(BQ+CQ) = AD+BC. For rectangle AB=CD and AD=BC, so 2AB = 2AD → AB = AD. All sides equal and all angles 90°, so it is a square.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित त्रिकोणमितीय सर्वसमिका सिद्ध कीजिए:
√((cosec A − 1)/(cosec A + 1)) = sec A − tan A
questions.text_english:
Prove the following trigonometric identity:
√((cosec A − 1)/(cosec A + 1)) = sec A − tan A

key_points: Multiply numerator and denominator inside the root by (cosec A − 1):
= 1/cos A − tan A = sec A − tan A = RHS

questions.solution: LHS = √((cosecA−1)/(cosecA+1)). Rationalise: = √((cosecA−1)²/(cosec²A−1)) = (cosecA−1)/cotA = cosecA/cotA − 1/cotA = secA − tanA = RHS.

questions.text: 200 पेनों के एक समूह में 180 पेन अच्छे हैं और बाकी के पेन खराब हैं। एक ग्राहक पेन जब ही खरीदता है जब वह खराब न हो। दुकानदार एक पेन इस समूह से यादृच्छया निकालता है और ग्राहक को देता है। ग्राहक इस पेन को नहीं खरीदेगा, इसकी प्रायिकता क्या है? 100 पेनों का एक और समूह है जिसमें 80 पेन अच्छे हैं, उसको 200 पेनों के पहले वाले समूह में मिला दिया जाता है। तत्पश्चात् दुकानदार अब पूरे समूह से एक पेन यादृच्छया निकालता है और इस पेन को ग्राहक को देता है। ग्राहक इस पेन को खरीदेगा, इसकी प्रायिकता क्या है?
questions.text_english: A lot consists of 200 pens of which 180 are good and the rest are defective. A customer will buy a pen if it is not defective. The shopkeeper draws a pen at random and gives it to the customer. What is the probability that the customer will not buy it? Another lot of 100 pens containing 80 good pens is mixed with the previous lot of 200 pens. The shopkeeper now draws one pen at random from the entire lot and gives it to the customer. What is the probability that the customer will buy the pen?

key_points: After mixing: total pens = 200 + 100 = 300. Good pens = 180 + 80 = 260.

questions.solution: P(not buy from first lot) = 20/200 = 1/10. After mixing: 300 total pens, 260 good. P(buy) = 260/300 = 13/15.

questions.text:
(क) सिद्ध कीजिए कि √3 एक अपरिमेय संख्या है।

अथवा

(ख) संख्या x का गुणखंड वृक्ष नीचे दिखाया गया है। x, y, a और b के मान ज्ञात कीजिए। अत: संख्या x को अभाज्य गुणखंडों के गुणनफल के रूप में व्यक्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Prove that √3 is an irrational number.

sub_questions.text: Prove that √3 is an irrational number.
sub_questions.text_english: Prove that √3 is an irrational number.

key_points: Assume √3 is rational. Then √3 = p/q where p and q are coprime integers and q ≠ 0.
So 3 divides p². Since 3 is prime, 3 divides p. Let p = 3k.
Then 9k² = 3q² → q² = 3k² → 3 divides q² → 3 divides q.
But then 3 divides both p and q, contradicting that p and q are coprime.

sub_questions.solution: Assume √3 = p/q (coprime). Then p² = 3q², so 3|p. Let p=3m; then 3m² = q², so 3|q. This contradicts p, q being coprime. Hence √3 is irrational.

questions.solution: Polynomial = x² − 5x − 6. Factorising: (x−6)(x+1) = 0. Zeroes are x = 6 and x = −1.

questions.text_english:
State "Basic Proportionality Theorem" and use it to prove the following:
A line through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.

key_points: Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT/Thales' Theorem): If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
Given: In △ABC, D is the midpoint of AB and DE ∥ BC, where E is on AC.
To prove: E is the midpoint of AC (AE = EC).
Since D is midpoint of AB: AD = DB → AD/DB = 1.
Hence E is the midpoint of AC.

questions.solution: BPT: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, it divides them in the same ratio. Given D is midpoint of AB, DE ∥ BC. By BPT: AD/DB = AE/EC. Since AD = DB, AD/DB = 1, so AE = EC, i.e., E bisects AC.

sub_questions.text: The difference of the squares of two positive numbers is 180. The square of the smaller number is 8 times the greater number. Find the two numbers.
sub_questions.text_english: The difference of the squares of two positive numbers is 180. The square of the smaller number is 8 times the greater number. Find the two numbers.

key_points: Let the greater number be x and smaller be y.

sub_questions.solution: Let greater = x, smaller = y. x² − y² = 180 and y² = 8x. So x² − 8x − 180 = 0 → (x−18)(x+10) = 0 → x = 18. y² = 144 → y = 12.
